exercises.prompt: What did the Prophet say he was sent to perfect?

source.text: I was sent only to perfect good character.

exercises.prompt: What did the Prophet say happens to the one who humbles himself for Allah?
exercises.explanation: Tawadu is strength disguised as lowliness: no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah elevates him.

source.text: No one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him.

exercises.prompt: What did the Prophet say is placed on the believer’s scale heavier than anything?
exercises.explanation: On the Day of Judgement the scales weigh character - daily kindness can outweigh impressive feats.

source.text: Nothing is placed on the scales heavier than good character.

exercises.prompt: What image does the Quran use for how you should treat your parents?
exercises.explanation: The wings of mercy replace the wings you had as a child - the parent-child role reverses with age.

source.text: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say: My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small.

options.text: Stand above them to guide them
Decide for them without consulting them

exercises.prompt: Your elderly parent asks something that frustrates you. What did Allah explicitly forbid?
exercises.explanation: The Quran names the smallest irritation - uff - and forbids it. Anything harsher is already far past the line.

source.text: Do not say to them "uff", nor repel them, but speak to them a noble word.

options.text: Even saying "uff" (a word of annoyance) to them

exercises.prompt: A man asked the Prophet: who deserves my best companionship? What did he answer?
